subject: Business Models
title: Auction Fees
description: A quick win: understand Auction Fees.

hook.text: Christie's sold a digital artwork for $69 million and kept over $10 million in fees.

buildup.text: Auction houses charge 'buyer's premium' (13-25%) on top of the hammer price, plus seller commissions.

discovery.text: Both buyer and seller pay. The auction house earns from both sides of every transaction.

twist.text: eBay disrupted physical auctions online but uses the same two-sided fee model: list and sell.

climax.text: Auctions work when price discovery is valuable—when neither side knows what something is worth.

punchline.text: Both sides pay the auctioneer. Uncertainty creates the fee.

quiz.question: Why do auction models charge both buyers and sellers?

details.summary: Auction fees are charges levied by auction platforms on each completed sale. eBay charges listing fees and takes a percentage of the final sale price. Google Ads charges per click in a real-time ad auction. Sotheby's takes a buyer's premium of up to 25% on art and collectible sales.
details.whyItMatters: Auction platforms extract value from the price discovery process they facilitate. By bringing competitive bidders together, they increase seller revenue and can justify significant fees for the liquidity and trust their marketplace provides.
takeaways: Platforms charge fees for facilitating competitive bidding processes
Fees may include listing charges, success fees, and buyer premiums
Auction platforms earn more as competition drives prices higher

faq.question: How do online ad auction fees generate billions in revenue?
faq.answer: Google and Meta run real-time auctions for every ad impression. Advertisers bid on keywords and audiences. The auction selects winners and sets prices billions of times daily. Google Ads generated over 230 billion in 2023, making it the largest auction system in economic history.

faq.question: Why do auction houses charge both buyers and sellers?
faq.answer: Buyer premiums of 15-25% are charged to buyers above the hammer price. Sellers pay commissions of 5-20% depending on the sale price. Charging both sides maximizes revenue from the price discovery service the auction house provides through its reputation, expertise, and buyer network.
